_comment: Tax return result template. Only sections relevant to the taxpayer's situation are included. Field names MUST match what generate_tax_pdf.py expects.

meta._note_exchange_rates: Keys are currency codes, e.g. {"EUR": 1.08}. generate_tax_pdf.py reads this first, falls back to exchange_rate_* keys.
meta._note_integrity: Skills should update _last_modified_by (skill name) and _last_modified_at (ISO timestamp) on every write. Subsequent skills should verify these fields to detect unexpected modifications.
meta._note_limitations: C2 manifest: what this return does NOT cover, copied verbatim from the /tax-compute capability gate (python3 agents/lib/capabilities.py --workspace . --json → limitations). /tax-generate prints it on page 1. Never empty after compute — it always carries at least the state-scope note.

social_security_worksheet._note: Persist every actual compute_taxable_ss input after computing line 6b. Confirm only a regular worksheet without lump-sum election or combined IRA/MAGI-dependent adjustment feedback. Required by income scenarios and Roth sweeps; never infer gross benefits from the taxable amount. See docs/contributing/social-security-planning.md.

form_1040._note_digital_asset: Form 1040 page-1 attestation. MUST be 'Yes' if the taxpayer received (reward/award/payment) OR sold/exchanged/disposed of any digital asset. /tax-parse-crypto sets this. Buying-and-holding with USD only is 'No'.
form_1040._note_line_1h: 1040 line 1h — other earned income NOT on a W-2. J2: a DISQUALIFYING ESPP disposition's ordinary component goes here when the employer W-2 did NOT already include it (common for former employees); do NOT double-add if the W-2 already includes it. line_1z_total_wages = sum of lines 1a–1h.
form_1040._note_schedule_e_k1_income: GROSS POSITIVE partnership / S-corp K-1 distributive income the return reflects — the PTET-ELIGIBLE pass-through-entity income only. EXCLUDE Schedule E rental real estate and royalty income (not a qualifying PTET entity), and DO NOT net against other entities' K-1 LOSSES (the PTET base is per-entity: a $200K profitable CA K-1 alongside a separate $100K loss is a real $200K PTET base, so record $200K here, not the $100K net). Sum the positive qualifying K-1 shares. /tax-ptet's phantom-income guard compares supplied --income against THIS figure (not the aggregate line 8, which folds in unemployment / taxable refunds / Sch C / gambling), so unrelated Schedule-1 income can't mask a K-1 that isn't in the return, while a legitimate per-entity PTET claim isn't blocked by an unrelated Schedule E loss. 0 when there is no qualifying K-1 income.
form_1040._note_line_13b: OBBBA Schedule 1-A total (tips + overtime premium + car-loan interest + enhanced senior), a BELOW-AGI deduction. Line 14 = 12 + 13a + 13b + 13c. Never in line 10 (would wrongly cut AGI). See the schedule_1a section.
form_1040._note_line_13c: OBBBA §170(p) non-itemizer charitable deduction (compute_charitable_non_itemizer, TY2026+). A BELOW-AGI deduction for STANDARD-deduction filers only ($1,000/$2,000-MFJ cap; cash gifts, no DAF/§509(a)(3)). Included in line 14, NOT in AGI, and reduces the Form 8995 taxable-income-before-QBI base like 13b. $0 for itemizers (they use Schedule A charitable) and pre-TY2026. See the charitable_non_itemizer section. (Verify the final TY2026 form line placement and rename if the IRS assigns a different line.)
form_1040._note_line_17: Form 1040 line 17 = Schedule 2 Part I. Line 1 is the Form 6251 AMT; line 2 is excess advance premium tax credit, which the capability gate BLOCKS, so in practice this is form_6251.amt. It has to be a FIELD: line 18 = 16 + 17 is the base the CTC Credit Limit Worksheet and line 22 both read, and with no line 17 an AMT filer's line 22 and line 24 were the regular tax alone — the AMT dropped off the return entirely, understating total tax for exactly the ISO exerciser Form 6251 is included for. Derived by agents/lib/return_builder.py; do not type it.
form_1040._note_line_27: Form 1040 line 27 — the Earned Income Credit. NOT COMPUTED by this toolkit: nothing in agents/lib calculates it, federally or for New York. FOUR lines carry it and each has its OWN form — this one, IT-201 line 65 (Form IT-215), line 66 (Form IT-209, noncustodial parent) and line 70 (the NYC EIC); never copy one onto another. The field exists so a figure the taxpayer worked out elsewhere has somewhere to land and reaches line 33; leaving it 0 for an eligible filer silently understates the refund, and NO downstream check can catch that — the tie-out compares source documents against the return and a credit has none. What is disclosed instead: flags.may_qualify_for_eic (asked by the /tax-setup interview) puts the capability gate's `earned_income_credit` rule on meta.limitations, and the tie-out advises by line while any of the four still records 0. Take the figure from tax software or the EIC worksheet in the 1040 instructions, never from a guess. See docs/contributing/tax-gotchas.md.
form_1040._note_line_28: Form 1040 line 28 — the refundable Additional Child Tax Credit, which IS computed: compute_child_tax_credit() splits into nonrefundable_used (line 19) and refundable_actc (this line). It had no field at all until V1's second slice, so the computed figure was thrown away and line 33 omitted it — understating the refund for exactly the families the ACTC exists for, and understating the refundable credits amend.py derives as line 33 minus 25d minus 26 for Form 1040-X line 15. Derived into line 33 by agents/lib/return_builder.py; write the engine's refundable_actc here.
form_1040._note_refundable_aotc: Form 8863 line 8 (40% refundable AOTC) — flows into line_33 even at $0 tax. Persisted at the 1040 level (like the excess-SS note below) so /tax-generate and /tax-verify can audit the refundable payment instead of it silently folding into line 33.
form_1040._note_excess_ss: Schedule 3 line 11: per-person compute_excess_ss_withholding() excess_credit sum (multi-employer over the wage base). Flows into line_31_schedule3_part2 -> line_33. Persisted here so /tax-generate and /tax-verify can audit the refundable payment instead of it silently folding into line 33.
form_1040._note_line_36: Form 1040 line 36 — the part of an overpayment APPLIED to next year's estimated tax rather than refunded. Line 35a = line 34 minus this. It must not exceed line 34. /tax-rollover CARRIES it into next year's taxpayer_profile.json prior_year.estimated_payments_applied, and next year's derived-lines gate refuses a line 26 smaller than it — line 26 is "estimated tax payments AND amount applied from the prior-year return", one line carrying both, and the applied half is the one payment on it with no document behind it. Before this field the figure could not even be written down, so line 35a equalled line 34 for every filer who applied part of a refund forward.

_optional_sections_below: Include only if applicable to this taxpayer. Remove sections that don't apply.

schedule_1a._include_if: compute_schedule_1a ran and total > 0 (any of tips/overtime-premium/car-loan/senior allowed) — TY2025-2028 only (OBBBA)
schedule_1a.note: OBBBA Schedule 1-A deductions, BELOW AGI (line 13b). Copy compute_schedule_1a's NESTED per-provision objects here VERBATIM (each carries allowed / disallowed_by_cap / disallowed_by_phaseout) and ALSO record the raw input amount + magi, so the Schedule 1-A worksheet (lines 4-38) can be reconstructed/audited from result.json — not just the allowed totals. total → form_1040.line_13b_schedule_1a_deductions; senior.allowed → form_6251.senior_deduction (AMT addback). NOT in line 10 — these do not reduce AGI or any MAGI-gated computation.
schedule_1a._note_car_loan_detail: Schedule 1-A Part IV per-vehicle rows when car_loan.allowed > 0: [{vin, interest_paid, business_deducted}]. The car_loan_interest passed to compute_schedule_1a must be the PERSONAL-use portion NET of any vehicle interest already deducted on Schedule C/E/F (business_deducted) — passing gross double-deducts the business share and understates tax. /tax-generate --filing-package reads this for the Part IV detail.

charitable_non_itemizer._include_if: compute_charitable_non_itemizer ran and allowed > 0 (STANDARD-deduction filer, cash gifts, TY2026+)
charitable_non_itemizer.note: OBBBA §170(p) below-AGI charitable deduction for standard-deduction filers. allowed → form_1040.line_13c_charitable_non_itemizer (in line 14, NOT AGI; reduces the Form 8995 taxable-income-before-QBI base). Cash gifts only (no DAF/§509(a)(3)); no §70425 0.5% floor; no carryforward. $0 for itemizers and pre-TY2026.

schedule_a._include_if: compute_schedule_a ran and use_itemized is true, OR charitable_ledger is present, OR the election was close enough to document — within $500
schedule_a.note: Itemized deductions. Election computed by compute_schedule_a, not vibes.

schedule_ca_itemized._include_if: CA return and compute_ca_itemized ran; retain whenever charitable_ledger is present, including standard-deduction years
schedule_ca_itemized.note: CA Schedule CA itemized path. Independent of the federal election.

form_6251._include_if: has_iso_exercise flag is true, OR AMT applies, OR a prior-year Form 8801 carryforward exists
form_6251.note: AMT (v1: ISO-exerciser path). CA Schedule P NOT computed — see notes.
form_6251._note_iso_bargain: Input echo: sum of (box 4 FMV - box 3 strike) x box 5 shares across Form 3921s for shares HELD past year-end (same-year sales are W-2 income, not an AMT adjustment). The A2 tie-out compares the parse ledger's iso_bargain records against this figure.

form_2210._include_if: compute_form_2210 ran and no_penalty is false (an underpayment exists)
form_2210.note: Underpayment of estimated tax (1040 line 38). Computed by compute_form_2210 — regular method, even-withholding default; Schedule AI not modeled.

schedule_c._note_line_31: Positive = profit, negative = loss. Single field replaces dual profit/loss fields.

schedule_d._note_8949_code_b: Each box detail row carries a SIGNED `adjustment` (Form 8949 column (g)) with an `adjustment_code` (column (f), e.g. 'B'): negative reduces the gain. gain = proceeds − cost + adjustment. The `cost` field stays the BROKER-reported basis (column (e)) so /tax-verify and software transfer match the 1099-B; the correction lives in `adjustment`. The classic case is employer stock (RSU/ESPP/NQSO) whose 1099-B basis excludes the W-2-included compensation — set `adjustment_code` to 'B', set `employer_stock` to true, and apply the adjustment ONLY from a documented source (broker supplemental statement, Form 3922/3921, vest confirmation), never inferred. A covered Box A/D lot that carries ANY adjustment must be reported on Form 8949 (populate the `form_8949` arrays too) — the direct-to-Schedule-D shortcut is only for adjustment-free Box A/D lots. The tie-out sums ONLY rows with `employer_stock == true` — code 'B' is NOT unique to employer stock (a non-employer 1099-B basis correction also uses code B), so the boolean provenance marker (not the code alone) scopes the employer-stock reconciliation; a non-employer code-B correction on another lot therefore can't corrupt it. Row key → Schedule D line mapping: Box A → line 1a (no adj) / 1b (with adj, via 8949); Box B → line 2; Box C → line 3; Box D → line 8a (no adj) / 8b (with adj, via 8949); Box E → line 9; Box F → line 10. Box A/D = basis reported to IRS; Box B/E = basis not reported (foreign brokers); Box C/F = no 1099-B (no code-B adjustment).

loss_carryforward_to_next_year._comment: Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet (Schedule D instructions): unused net loss carried to next year, split by character (ST offsets ST first). /tax-compute fills this using the loss actually usable this year ($3,000 / $1,500 MFS cap, less when taxable income is lower); /tax-rollover prefers this explicit block over deriving from line_16_combined.

crypto_summary._note: Crypto is PROPERTY (Notice 2014-21): wash-sale (§1091) does NOT apply. FIFO basis, universal per-asset pool (v1). Capital rows feed form_8949/schedule_d; ordinary_income.total feeds Schedule 1 line 8 (Schedule C + SE tax if mining/staking is a business).

section_988_fx._include_if: a directly-held foreign-currency (non-USD) BOND was disposed of — compute_section_988 ran. One entry per bond in `dispositions`. NOT for funds (a fund is a PFIC — see the capability gate).
section_988_fx._note: §988/Reg. §1.988-2(b) split: exchange_gain_ordinary → Schedule 1 (ordinary, regardless of holding period — and US-SOURCE for a US resident per §988(a)(3), so NOT Form 1116 foreign-source income); market_gain_capital → Schedule D (short/long per capital_term, the >1-year calendar-anniversary rule §1222). The two are reported SEPARATELY — never netted into one figure. total_gain is derived from the two rounded reportables so they reconcile to the cent.

form_8621_pfic._include_if: has_pfic_taxable_event AND the §1291 computation was run (acknowledged + foreign_holdings_detail facts present). One entry per fund in `funds` from compute_pfic_1291. NOT for a buy-and-hold PFIC (reporting-only §1298(f)).
form_8621_pfic._note: §1291 excess-distribution / disposition tax (compute_pfic_1291, Form 8621 Part V). ordinary_income_current → 1040 ordinary income (taxed at normal rates); deferred_tax_total (prior PFIC years at each year's highest ordinary rate, §1291(c)(2)) + interest_total (§6621 daily, §1291(c)(3)) → total_1291_addon, an ADD-ON to Form 1040 TOTAL TAX line 24 (deferred tax to the LEFT of line 24, interest via Schedule 2 line 17p → line 23) — added AFTER nonrefundable credits, NOT folded into line 16 (which credits reduce) and NOT re-run through brackets. If any fund's `complete` is False (missing historical top rate / uncovered §6621 quarter / absent distribution history), the return is INCOMPLETE — do not file; keep the capability BLOCK.
form_8621_pfic._funds_schema: Each entry in `funds`: {fund_id (STABLE, DISTINCT id matching the foreign_holdings_detail.holdings entry — the Step 12.7 tie-out matches taxable no-election funds to computed results BY fund_id, so a taxable fund with no matching complete entry FAILS the gate), complete (bool), is_disposition (bool), total_1291_addon (deferred tax + interest), ordinary_income_current (the EXCESS-distribution current-year allocation, ordinary now), nonexcess_ordinary (the NON-excess normal-dividend portion of a distribution — compute_pfic_excess_distribution's ordinary_now — 0 for a disposition), disposition_ordinary_income (REQUIRED + > 0 for EVERY fund sold at a POSITIVE gain — pure-disposition AND same-year distribution+sale alike: the sale leg's compute_pfic_1291 ordinary_income_current (current-year + pre-PFIC ordinary from the sale, always > 0 for a gain), recorded separately so the tie-out can prove the sale itself was run through §1291 and not masked by a stray nonexcess_ordinary or a small distribution result; 0/omitted for a distribution-only fund or a loss/zero-gain sale), ...}. ALL THREE amount fields (total_1291_addon, ordinary_income_current, nonexcess_ordinary) MUST be present + finite + >=0 on every complete fund (0 valid). A loss disposition still writes a fund entry: {fund_id, is_disposition: true, disposition_result: 'loss', total_1291_addon: 0, ordinary_income_current: 0, nonexcess_ordinary: 0, complete: true}.
form_8621_pfic._addon_placement: The §1291 deferred tax (aggregate increases in tax for prior years) is entered on Form 1040 to the LEFT of line 24 and included in the line-24 total; the §6621 interest charge goes on Schedule 2 line 17p -> Schedule 2 Part II -> Form 1040 line 23 -> line 24. BOTH are additions to TOTAL TAX (line 24) AFTER nonrefundable credits — NEVER folded into line 16 (regular tax), which credits reduce. So line_16_regular_tax == form_1040.line_16_tax (NO add-on), and form_1040.line_24_total_tax == line_24_regular_total_tax (the counterfactual total tax WITHOUT the add-on) + total_1291_addon. Per IRS Instructions for Form 8621 (Rev. Dec 2025), Part V line 16.

foreign_source_income._note: Add named sub-keys per income source, e.g. bank_deposit_interest, savings_interest

form_8938_fatca._include_if: has_foreign_accounts flag is true — include even if not required (to document threshold analysis)

fbar_fincen_114._include_if: (has_foreign_accounts OR signature_authority_foreign_accounts flag is true) AND aggregate > $10K — signature-authority-only accounts count toward the aggregate and go on Part IV (31 CFR 1010.350)
fbar_fincen_114.note: Filed electronically at BSA E-Filing, not with tax return

form_1099r_401k_rollover._note_payer_tin: Payer TINs (EINs) are full numbers from the original 1099-R. Only INDIVIDUAL SSNs use last-4-only policy.

form_8995_qbi._include_if: has QBI income or REIT dividends

schedule_p._note: CA Schedule P (540) AMT — compute_ca_schedule_p (7% TMT, 25% exemption phase-out per R&TC §17062, exemption/phaseout_start from state.amt). ca_amt is ADDED to ca_total_tax. carryforward_to_next_year is the deferral-attributable (ISO) CA AMT credit rolled forward by /tax-rollover (a SEPARATE carryforward from the federal Form 8801).

california_540._note_excess_sdi: Form 540 line 74: per-person compute_excess_sdi() when 2+ employers over-withheld SDI. TY2024+ (SB 951 removed the wage ceiling): always 0 / not applicable.

florida_state._note: Affirmative absence, not an empty section: a FL client must see that $0 state tax is CORRECT, not a gap. No FL return artifact exists; the only computation here is the federal Schedule A line 5a sales-tax election input (compute_sales_tax_deduction -> compute_schedule_a state_local_sales_taxes). No computed-evidence pair on purpose — there is no computed state tax to protect from scaffold-reads (see docs/contributing/state-module-playbook.md, no-income-tax variant).
florida_state._note_no_income_tax_statement: Codex round-11 P2: this field ships null on purpose (not the affirmative sentence itself) so yoy_diff._section_present (keyed on this ONE field via INFORMATIONAL_SECTIONS) can tell a genuinely-computed FL section apart from an untouched/un-pruned template scaffold — a non-null default here would make EVERY result.json read as 'FL section present', even a CA taxpayer's file that was never pruned. /tax-compute's no-income-tax-states step writes the real statement text ('Florida imposes no personal income tax (Fla. Const. Art. VII, §5). No Florida individual income-TAX return exists or is required (Florida property and use-tax filings may still apply — see the use-tax note and property-tax items in this section for the specific forms). Wages, capital gains, retirement income, and interest/dividends are not state-taxed.') only when it actually computes for a FL (or other type-none) taxpayer. The parenthetical is deliberately form-NEUTRAL (Codex round-25 P2, matching tax-compute.md): the correct use-tax form depends on the dealer-registration answer (DR-15 for registered dealers, DR-15MO otherwise), so naming DR-15MO here unconditionally would contradict the tailored use_tax_note in the same result/PDF.
florida_state.use_tax_note: Florida self-assesses use tax on untaxed out-of-state/online purchases (6% + county surtax; the discretionary county surtax applies only to the first $5,000 of a single item, F.S. 212.054(2)(b)). Review whether any apply. If you are REGISTERED as a Florida sales-and-use-tax dealer, report and pay it on your regular Form DR-15 (registered dealers must NOT use DR-15MO, per floridarevenue.com's consumer use-tax guidance); otherwise use Form DR-15MO, the Out-of-State Purchase Return.

new_york_it201._note: Form IT-201, FULL-YEAR RESIDENT. The field names carry the FORM's line numbers because that is what /tax-verify ties against and what a taxpayer reading the return beside their software output can follow. Lines 19-33 come from compute_ny_agi, 39 from compute_ny_tax (the rate schedule PLUS the §601 benefit recapture, which is inside that function and not a caller's option), 43-46 from compute_ny_state_tax_total, 47-58 from compute_city_and_yonkers_total, and 76-82 from compute_ny_settlement. Lines 34-38 and 60 are the form's own arithmetic over those, assembled by /tax-compute step 10. NEVER reuse or overload california_540: the two sections are not interchangeable, and yoy_diff's mover list is keyed per section for exactly that reason.

additions._note: IT-201 lines 20-24. Line 23 is the IT-225 total, and its codes are recorded below so /tax-review can see WHICH additions were claimed rather than a lump sum. A-219 and A-222 are the PTET add-backs and are derived from the credits, never typed — see the ptet block.

subtractions._note: IT-201 lines 25-32. Line 29's pension-and-annuity exclusion is PER TAXPAYER and does not pool — neither spouse can claim any unused part of the other's — so it is recorded per person by compute_ny_pension_exclusion and only the total lands here.

new_york_it201._note_line_33: NEW YORK AGI MAY BE NEGATIVE and that is an ordinary return — line 33 has no floor, and a Schedule C loss, a K-1 loss or an NOL carryforward reaches it routinely. Only the individual modifications are floored.

it196._note: Form IT-196. INDEPENDENT of the federal election — New York lets a taxpayer itemize whether or not they did federally — and computed on federal rules AS THEY EXISTED BEFORE THE TCJA. Lines 1-45 are a NAMED NON-GOAL: compute_ny_itemized takes the pre-adjustment total as an INPUT and the federal Schedule A total is NOT a substitute for it. §615's two high-AGI reductions and the separate charitable limitation are what this block computes.

new_york_it201._note_line_36: DEPENDENTS ONLY. Tax Law §616 grants an exemption for each exemption allowed under IRC §151(c) — the dependent subsection. §151(b), the taxpayer and spouse, is not referenced: New York has NO personal exemption for either.
new_york_it201._note_line_39: tax_regime is "tax_table", "graduated", "entry_tier", "recapture_tier" or "full_recapture"; tax_schedule is the §601 schedule the filing status reads (a, b or c). Line 39 is NOT the state tax — lines 44 and 45 are still to come, and neither is derivable from compute_ny_tax's inputs.
new_york_it201._note_line_45: IT-201-ATT, and it is ADDED AFTER the nonrefundable credits have been capped at line 44. A credit cannot reduce it, so folding it in earlier would let one cancel the other.

nyc._note: New York City resident tax, IT-201 lines 47-54. City taxable income is the STATE's, except that a Charitable Gifts Trust deduction taken for the state is added back. Line 47a reads the City tax table while line 47 is under the fetched table ceiling and the City rate schedule at or above it. Beside 47a, 55 and 56 goes each function's `method`, as `<field>_method`: the tie-out fails a flagged line without it. A joint return with only ONE city resident REFUSES rather than taxing the household as residents, and so does a City resident for only part of the year: IT-360.1 is not modeled.

yonkers._include_if: a Yonkers resident, or nonresident with Yonkers earnings
yonkers._note: Yonkers has the same parity with the State residency test that the City has. Line 55 comes from compute_yonkers_resident_surcharge (the IT-201-I worksheet on line 46, for a WHOLE-year Yonkers resident), line 56 from compute_yonkers_nonresident_earnings_tax (Form Y-203 on a return that is not joint, line 6 limited to the resident surcharge). Lines 50 and 57 are the PART-YEAR city and Yonkers lines and belong to IT-360.1 — a named non-goal for this full-year-resident module.

mctmt._include_if: self-employment net earnings in the MCTD
mctmt._note: The metropolitan commuter transportation mobility tax rides this return for self-employed filers. TWO ZONES — geography, not income — with DIFFERENT rates, and the threshold is a per-zone CLIFF: over it, the WHOLE amount is taxed, not the excess. Neither zone's rate may stand in for the other's.

new_york_it201._note_line_58: Line 58 adds the MCTMT and both Yonkers taxes AFTER the two city credit caps, the same pattern as line 45 on the state side. compute_city_and_yonkers_total takes the three household flags and REFUSES a flagged line 47a, 55 or 56 nobody computed. Those three lines ship null, not 0, so one nobody computed stays visibly uncomputed, and the tie-out gate fails a return whose profile flags one while it is still null or absent: a line 58 assembled without the function, or typed here, cannot read it as $0.
new_york_it201._note_line_59: NOT COMPUTED, and null on purpose rather than 0. New York reports sales and use tax on untaxed out-of-state and online purchases ON THE INCOME TAX RETURN, and it changes the amount owed. A silent 0 would assert an answer nobody gave. /tax-compute asks, records the answer in answers.md, and records the limitation when the taxpayer cannot state one.

refundable_credits_and_payments._note: IT-201 lines 63-75. EVERY remaining New York credit is REFUNDABLE and belongs here with the payments, not above line 44 — and that includes the IT-653 PTET credit, whose excess is "treated as an overpayment, to be credited or refunded". The AMOUNT of each of these is a NAMED NON-GOAL: IT-213, IT-216, IT-215, IT-214 and IT-272 each carry their own worksheet, and compute_ny_settlement takes the figures as inputs. Where each one LANDS is settled; what each one IS, is not.

new_york_it201._note_penalties: The estimated tax penalty reduces an OVERPAYMENT where there is one and is included in the amount owed where there is not — it is never a separate bill beside the figure on line 80.

ptet._include_if: the taxpayer is an owner of an electing pass-through entity
ptet._note: Form IT-653. The credit and its IT-225 add-back are an EXACT PAIR: A-219 is the amount of the credit claimed on IT-653 LINE 1 and A-222 the amount on LINE 2. They do not combine, and claiming a credit without its addition under-states New York tax by the whole of the credit. The add-backs above are DERIVED from these figures, never typed.

estimated_tax_next_year._include_if: the taxpayer will owe New York estimated tax
estimated_tax_next_year._note: Form IT-2105, EQUAL QUARTERS — April, June, September and the following January, one voucher covering NYS, NYC, Yonkers and the MCTMT together. The required annual payment is the LESSER of the current-year and prior-year floors, the higher prior-year share keyed to NEW YORK adjusted gross income with married-filing-separately at its own threshold. The instalments SUM to the required payment: the last one absorbs the rounding remainder.

north_carolina_d400._note: Form D-400, FULL-YEAR RESIDENT, with Schedule S Parts A-B and the NC Schedule A. Maintained contract: docs/contributing/state-module-nc.md (result and registration). Field names carry the D-400 LINE NUMBERS because that is what /tax-verify ties against. Lines 13, 21c, 21d, 22 and 24 are part-year/nonresident (Schedule PN) or amended-return lines and are ABSENT on purpose. Amounts are carried in CENTS as the engine computes them (AGENTS.md §8); the D-400 itself is filed in whole dollars (D-401 p.4), so a whole-dollar transcription may differ by under a dollar a line. NEVER reuse or overload california_540 or new_york_it201.
north_carolina_d400._note_line_6: Federal AGI (Form 1040 line 11). North Carolina reads the Code as of state.irc_conformity_date, and every difference reaches the return through Schedule S, never by editing this line.
north_carolina_d400._note_line_10: 10a counts the children for whom a FEDERAL child tax credit (IRC §24) was allowed — never the dependent count, an 'other dependent' is not a §24 child. 10b reads the child-deduction table on FEDERAL AGI (line 6), not on NC income.
north_carolina_d400._note_line_11: line_11_method is "standard" or "itemized". Line 11 MAY BE ZERO on a computed return — a married-filing-separately filer whose spouse itemizes, or a filer not eligible for the federal standard deduction — so a zero here is not by itself an uncomputed section.
north_carolina_d400._note_line_14: Equals line 12b for a full-year resident and MAY BE NEGATIVE; line 15 floors the TAX at zero, not this line.
north_carolina_d400._note_line_18: An INPUT or a CERTIFICATION, never derived: the taxpayer states the use tax due on untaxed out-of-state and online purchases (line_18_use_tax), or certifies none is due (use_tax_none_due_circle true, line 18 then 0). Both ship null on purpose rather than 0 or false — North Carolina reports use tax ON THE INCOME TAX RETURN and it changes the amount owed, so a silent 0 would assert an answer nobody gave. Left unanswered, both stay null and the amount due excludes use tax; /tax-compute asks, and records the limitation when the taxpayer cannot state one.
north_carolina_d400._note_line_26: 26b-26d are the late-filing and late-payment penalties and interest; 26e is the Form D-422 interest on underpaid estimated tax, an INPUT rather than computed. Line 27 is 26a + 26d + 26e, and line 28 subtracts 26e from an overpayment.
north_carolina_d400._note_line_29: Lines 29-32 are the taxpayer's contributions and amount applied to next year's estimated tax, passed through as inputs; line 33 is their total.
north_carolina_d400._note_circles: The D-400 page 1 circles. An automatic federal extension extends the North Carolina return ONLY when the 'Federal Extension' circle is filled (D-401 p.7); without it an extended return is delinquent. Both ship null — unanswered — rather than false, which would assert that no extension was taken.

schedule_s._include_if: any Schedule S addition or deduction
schedule_s._note: D-400 Schedule S. Only the lines in v1 scope are fields; every other line is a named non-goal on meta.limitations (spec §8). Line 16 is the Part A total that lands on D-400 line 7, line 41 the Part B total that lands on line 9.

schedule_a._include_if: line_11_method is "itemized", or the NC itemized total was compared
schedule_a._note: The NC Schedule A, INDEPENDENT of the federal election and computed from RAW inputs under the Code state.irc_conformity_date names — never copied from the federal Schedule A, which is wrong in both directions for North Carolina (spec §2). No state or local income or sales tax line exists. Line 4 is the combined mortgage-interest-plus-property-tax cap, household-wide even for married filing separately.

income_summary_by_person._note: IMPORTANT: Replace 'primary'/'spouse' keys with actual lowercase first names (e.g., 'john'/'jane'). generate_tax_pdf.py reads DATA['income_summary_by_person']['john'] — keys MUST match. Sub-fields are taxpayer-specific: add only income types that apply (e.g., 'interest_foreign' for foreign interest, 'consulting_gross' for Schedule C). The PDF generator uses .get(key, 0) so missing sub-fields default to $0.

form_8863._note: Form 8863 education credits — computed by compute_education_credits. nonrefundable_credit_schedule3_line3 flows to Schedule 3 line 3 (and reduces the CTC Credit Limit Worksheet amount); refundable_aotc_line29 flows to Form 1040 line 29 (payments — pays out at $0 tax). Per-student AOTC eligibility facts (half-time, first 4 years, <4 prior claims, no felony drug conviction) are user-asserted; qualified expenses are NET of tax-free scholarships/employer assistance/529 earnings per Pub 970.

form_8606._include_if: has_backdoor_roth or has_roth_conversion is true, OR either individual has nondeductible traditional-IRA basis (prior_year.ira_basis_by_taxpayer or confirmed legacy ira_basis) or a nondeductible contribution this year
form_8606._note: Use compute_individual_8606 and replace this scaffold with its whole returned block. schema individual-8606/v1, inputs and by_taxpayer hold independent primary/spouse worksheets. Only gross_to_1040 and taxable_to_1040 are summed to 4a/4b. Each basis_remaining rolls to that owner in prior_year.ira_basis_by_taxpayer. Flat lines below are legacy single-person fields; never fill them as a household worksheet.

ira_contribution._note_ca_savings: CA-only field — /tax-setup removes it for non-CA taxpayers.

balance_due_summary._note_california_refund: CA-only legacy field — /tax-setup removes it for non-CA taxpayers; other states' balances live in their own state section.
